compatibility.detail: Wire change is additive: the outcome-history response gains an echoed mission field and accepts a mission query parameter. Daemons that predate it ignore the parameter and return the unfiltered page with 200, so a new CLI passing --mission requires the echoed mission field and otherwise fails with "this daemon does not support --mission; upgrade the daemon" (text and --json). CLI output adds a scope line to history pages and window/full-history lines to mission summaries. Older CLIs keep working against new daemons. Mixed-version paging must stay on one daemon: history cursors remain local to the serving daemon.

manual.detail: No action required. To page one mission's terminal history: fractal missions ls --all --mission <id> [--status failed] [--since 6h] [--cursor ...]. For running and waiting runs, read /v1/mission-runs?mission=<id>.

recovery.detail: No persisted state changes; ordinary binary rollback applies.

replay.detail: No replay change; outcome history still reads terminal transition claims in canonical claim-index order, with the same reason recovery.

rules.detail: No admission or authority change. mission on outcome history accepts an identity- or canonical-named mission; work collection filters by the owning mission of step-run subjects. --mission cannot combine with --watch.

schema.detail: No SQL migration and no new index. A mission page starts from an index search on mission_runs.mission_id (the mission's run subjects plus their step-run subjects via step_runs_run_index) and reaches claims through claims_subject_kind_index, so it reads only that mission's claims; unfiltered pages still walk the terminal-history index.

summary: Outcome history pages one mission's terminal transitions: mission on Store::outcome_history, GET /v1/outcome-history, and fractal missions ls --all --mission <id> (composes with --status/--since/--until/--cursor). Mission summaries and published list cards now say their run previews are windows and point at the full-history read.
